VIRGIN ISLANDS
STATUTORY INSTRUMENT 2014 NO. 83
STATUS OF CHILDREN ACT, 2014
(No. 6 of 2014)
Status of Children (Parentage Testing Procedure) Regulations,
2014
[Gazetted 6th November, 2014]
The Minister, in exercise of the powers conferred by section 19 of
the Status of Children Act, 2014 makes the following Regulations:
Citation. 1. These Regulations may be cited as the Status of
Children (Parentage Testing Procedure) Regulations, 2014.
Interpretation 2. In these Regulations
.
No. 6 of 2014 “Act” means the Status of Children Act, 2014;
“approved laboratory” means a laboratory approved by the
Minister under the Act for the purpose of carrying out a
parentage testing procedure;
“donor” means a person required to provide a sample for the
purposes of a parentage testing procedure;
“report” means a report made in accordance with regulation 12;
“sample” includes tissue, fluid or any other form of substance
naturally occurring in or on the human body and taken from
a person for the purpose of a parentage testing procedure;
“sample collector” means a person who takes a sample;
“testing” means the implementation, or part of the implementation,
of a parentage testing procedure.
3. A parentage testing procedure is carried out in
Parentage
testing accordance with the Act and these Regulations if it is

comply
(a) in compliance with regulations 4 to 11;

12.

person Collector.

(b) is employed by a hospital, an approved

the purpose of taking a sample.

who is responsible for the care, protection and welfare of that
donor.
Collection of 6. (1) A sample collector may take a sample of blood
blood from a donor only with a needle or syringe that
samples.
(a) has not been used for any other purpose;
(b) is sterilised; and
(c) is disposable.
(2) Before taking a sample of blood from a donor, the
sample collector shall ensure that the area of the donor’s skin into
which the needle is to be inserted to withdraw the blood has been
cleaned with an antiseptic.
Collection of 7. (1) This regulation applies to the taking of a sample,
samples for except a sample of blood, from the donor for the purposes of a
DNA typing. parentage testing procedure that is DNA typing.
(2) A sample collector shall take a sample from a donor
only with a swab that has not been used for any other purpose and
has been sterilised.
(3) A sample collector shall take a sample that is a skin
scraping or a hair root only with an implement designed for the
purpose and that has been sterilised before use.
Container 8. (1) If a sample is taken from a donor, the sample
to be sealed collector shall ensure that
and labelled.
(a) the sample is placed in a container
(i) immediately after it is taken; and
(ii) in the presence of the donor;
(b) the container has not previously been used
for any other purpose;
(c) the container is sealed in a way that, if it
were opened after being sealed, that fact
4

would be evident on inspection of the
container;
(d) the container is labelled in a way that, if it
were opened after being sealed, that fact
would be evident on inspection of the
container;
(e) the particulars on the label are inscribed in
ink and include
(i) the full name of the donor; and
(ii) the date and time at which the
sample was taken; and
(f) when paragraph (e) is complied with, the
sample collector and the donor sign the label
in ink.
(2) If the donor is under the age of eighteen years, the
procedures specified in subregulation (1) (a) and (f) must be
completed in the presence of the person who is responsible for the
care, protection and welfare of the donor.
(3) If the donor is suffering from a mental disability
(a) the procedure as specified in subregulation
(1) (a), may be completed in the presence of
the person who is responsible for the care,
protection and welfare of the donor; and
(b) the procedure referred to in subregulation
(1) (f), shall be taken to be complied with
only if the label is signed by a person who is
responsible for the care, protection and
welfare of the donor.
9. After taking a sample from the donor, the sample Statement
collector shall by Sample
Collector.

Schedule
Form No. 3 in the Schedule; Form No. 3

the photograph; and
(c) sign his or her name partly on the
photograph and partly in a way that, if the
photograph were later removed from the
statement, the removal would be evident
from inspection of the statement.
Packing and 10. (1) A sample shall be packed, stored and transported to
storage an approved laboratory for testing in a manner that
requirements.
(a) will preserve the integrity of the sample; and
(b) ensures that the testing of the sample will
produce the same results as would have been
obtained if the sample had been tested
immediately after collection.
(2) The sample collector shall ensure that the following
documents are sent to the approved laboratory with the sample:
(a) the affidavit completed under regulation 5
(1) (a);
(b) the declaration completed under regulation 5
(2);
(c) the statement completed under regulation 9.
Testing 11. An approved laboratory to which a sample has been
samples. sent for testing shall ensure that the testing is completed using
scientifically accepted parentage testing procedures.
12. (1) For the purposes of section 11 of the Act, a report
Reports.
Form No. 4 shall be prepared in the form set out as Form No. 4 in the
Schedule Schedule.
(2) Part 1 of the report must be completed by the
Director of the approved laboratory or a designated person.
(3) Part 2 of the report must be completed by the person
(a) who carried out the parentage testing
procedure; or
6

(b) under whose supervision the parentage
testing procedure was carried out.
(4) A report completed otherwise than in accordance
with the Act and this regulation shall be of no effect.
13. (1) A fee shall be payable in respect of instruments
Fees.
filed in the Registry pursuant to section 7 of the Act.
(2) For an instrument filed under section 5 (1) (f) or (g)
of the Act, the fee payable shall be the appropriate fee as
prescribed in PART 37 of the Schedule (Registration And Records
Fees - Registration and Records Act (Cap. 67)) to the Statutory
Rates, Fees and Charges Act, 2005.
